blocks.html: Jonah runs from God (and is swallowed by a fish)

items.html: Now the word of the LORD came unto Jonah the son of Amittai, saying,
Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me.

blocks.html:
The word of God came to Jonah and said,

Go to Nineveh and cry against it,

because I've heard about its wickedness.

items.html: But Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the LORD, and went down to Joppa; and he found a ship going to Tarshish: so he paid the fare thereof, and went down into it, to go with them unto Tarshish from the presence of the LORD.

blocks.html:
So Jonah fled from the presence of God. [1]

He went to Joppa and boarded a ship bound for Tarshish.

items.html: But the LORD sent out a great wind into the sea, and there was a mighty tempest in the sea, so that the ship was like to be broken.

blocks.html:
But God sent a storm on the sea,

which threatened to sink the ship.

items.html: Then the mariners were afraid, and cried every man unto his god, and cast forth the wares that were in the ship into the sea, to lighten it of them. But Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep.

blocks.html:
The crew threw things overboard to lighten the ship,

while Jonah slept below deck.

items.html: So the shipmaster came to him, and said unto him, What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us, that we perish not.

blocks.html:
The captain came to Jonah and said,

Get up and ask your God to save us.

items.html: And they said every one to his fellow, Come, and let us cast lots, that we may know for whose cause this evil is upon us. So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.

blocks.html:
Meanwhile the crew cast lots to find the source of the evil. [2]

And the lot fell upon Jonah.

items.html: Then said they unto him, Tell us, we pray thee, for whose cause this evil is upon us; What is thine occupation? and whence comest thou? what is thy country? and of what people art thou?

blocks.html:
So they asked Jonah,

Why is the storm coming from you?

items.html: And he said unto them, I am an Hebrew; and I fear the LORD, the God of heaven, which hath made the sea and the dry land.

blocks.html:
Jonah said,

I'm a Hebrew. I think God is after me.

items.html: Then were the men exceedingly afraid, and said unto him. Why hast thou done this? For the men knew that he fled from the presence of the LORD, because he had told them.
Then said they unto him, What shall we do unto thee, that the sea may be calm unto us? for the sea wrought, and was tempestuous.

blocks.html:
The sailors said to Jonah,

Why have you done this?

(They knew he was fleeing from God, because he told them.)

What should we do to you, so the sea will be calm?

items.html: And he said unto them, Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm unto you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you.
Nevertheless the men rowed hard to bring it to the land; but they could not: for the sea wrought, and was tempestuous against them.

blocks.html:
Jonah said,

Throw me overboard. [3]

items.html: Wherefore they cried unto the LORD, and said, We beseech thee, O LORD, we beseech thee, let us not perish for this man's life, and lay not upon us innocent blood: for thou, O LORD, hast done as it pleased thee.

blocks.html:
The sailors cried to God, saying

We know you want to kill this man.

Please don't kill us too.

items.html: So they look up Jonah, and cast him forth into the sea: and the sea ceased from her raging.
Then the men feared the LORD exceedingly, and offered a sacrifice unto the LORD, and made vows.

blocks.html:
So they threw Jonah overboard. [4]

And the sea became calm.

items.html: Now the LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

blocks.html:
A great fish swallowed Jonah,

and he was in the fish's belly for three days and three nights.

footnotes.html:
Jonah rose up to flee ... from the presence of the LORD. (v.3)

(There are some places where God can't find you.)

Does God know and see everything?

Let us cast lots, that we may know for whose cause this evil is upon us. (v.7)

The sailors cast lots to see who was causing the storm.

And it worked, too (casting lots always does in the Bible), since the lot fell on Jonah.

Cast me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm. (v.12)

Jonah believes that by throwing himself into the sea, the storm will die down. And it worked!

So they look up Jonah, and cast him forth into the sea: and the sea ceased from her raging. (v.15)

Who cast Jonah into the sea?

The LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. (v.17)

God makes "a great fish" to swallow Jonah. And Jonah stayed in the fish's belly for three days and three nights.

Was Jonah swallowed by a fish or a whale?

blocks.html: Jonah's prayer from the fish's belly

items.html: Then Jonah prayed unto the LORD his God out of the fish's belly,

blocks.html: Jonah prayed in the fish's belly, saying,

items.html: And said, I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the LORD, and he heard me; out of the belly of hell cried I, and thou heardest my voice.

blocks.html: I'm praying to you from the belly of hell.

items.html: For thou hadst cast me into the deep, in the midst of the seas; and the floods compassed me about: all thy billows and thy waves passed over me.
Then I said, I am cast out of thy sight; yet I will look again toward thy holy temple.
The waters compassed me about, even to the soul: the depth closed me round about, the weeds were wrapped about my head.
I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with her bars was about me for ever: yet hast thou brought up my life from corruption, O LORD my God.
When my soul fainted within me I remembered the LORD: and my prayer came in unto thee, into thine holy temple.
They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy.

blocks.html: You threw me into the sea. [1]

items.html: But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed. Salvation is of the LORD.

blocks.html: So I'll sacrifice to you in thanksgiving.

items.html: And the LORD spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.

blocks.html:
Then God spoke to the fish

and it vomited Jonah on the dry land.

footnotes.html:
Thou hadst cast me into the deep. (v.3)

Who cast Jonah into the sea?

blocks.html: Jonah preaches to Nineveh

items.html: And the word of the LORD came unto Jonah the second time, saying,

blocks.html: The word of God came to Jonah the second time, saying,

items.html: Arise, go unto Nineveh, that great city, and preach unto it the preaching that I bid thee.

blocks.html: Go to Nineveh and preach to it.

items.html: So Jonah arose, and went unto Nineveh, according to the word of the LORD. Now Nineveh was an exceeding great city of three days' journey.

blocks.html:
So Jonah went to Nineveh.

(Nineveh was a huge city, three days' journey across.) [1]

items.html: And Jonah began to enter into the city a day's journey, and he cried, and said, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.

blocks.html:
When he entered the city, he cried out saying,

Nineveh will be overthrown in forty days. [2]
Everyone (man and beast) fasts and puts on sackcloth

items.html: So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them.

blocks.html: So everyone in Nineveh believed God, proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth. [3]

items.html: For word came unto the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, and he laid his robe from him, and covered him with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.

blocks.html: The king of Nineveh put on sackcloth and sat in ashes.

items.html: And he caused it to be proclaimed and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste any thing: let them not feed, nor drink water:

blocks.html:
And proclaimed a decree, saying,

No one in the kingdom, man or beast, will eat anything or drink any water.

items.html: But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily unto God: yea, let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands.

blocks.html: And everyone, including the animals, must cover themselves with sackcloth and cry out to God. [4]

items.html: Who can tell if God will turn and repent, and turn away from his fierce anger, that we perish not?

blocks.html:
Who knows?

Maybe God will repent and not kill us all.
God repents

items.html: And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not.

blocks.html: And God repented of the evil he said he'd do to them. [5]

footnotes.html:
Nineveh was an exceeding great city of three days' journey. (v.3)

That would make it about 60 miles in diameter -- larger than Los Angeles!

Jonah ... cried, and said, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown. (v.4)

Jonah prophesies that in forty days Nineveh shall be overthrown.

But it didn't happen because God repented (v.10).

So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them. (v.5)

Everyone in Nineveh turned to God. Jonah must be one hell of a preacher!

Let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily unto God. (v.8)

Even the animals converted and put on sackcloth when they heard Jonah preach!

God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not. (v.10)

Does God repent?

blocks.html: Jonah is angry with God (for not destroying Nineveh)

items.html: But it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was very angry.

blocks.html: But Jonah was exceedingly angry at God for not destroying Nineveh. [1]

items.html: And he prayed unto the LORD, and said, I pray thee, O LORD, was not this my saying, when I was yet in my country? Therefore I fled before unto Tarshish: for I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repentest thee of the evil.

blocks.html:
So he prayed to God, saying,

I knew you wouldn't destroy Nineveh,

so I fled from you to Tarshish.

items.html: Therefore now, O LORD, take, I beseech thee, my life from me; for it is better for me to die than to live.

blocks.html:
Go ahead and kill me.

It's better for me to die than to live.

items.html: Then said the LORD, Doest thou well to be angry?
So Jonah went out of the city, and sat on the east side of the city, and there made him a booth, and sat under it in the shadow, till he might see what would become of the city.

blocks.html:
Then God said to Jonah,

Do you think it's a good idea for you to be angry with me?

So Jonah went to the east side of the city, made a booth, and waited to see what would happen to the city.
God makes (and destroys) a gourd for Jonah

items.html: And the LORD God prepared a gourd, and made it to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shadow over his head, to deliver him from his grief. So Jonah was exceeding glad of the gourd.

blocks.html:
God made a gourd and put it over Jonah's head to shade him. [2]

Jonah was exceedingly happy with the gourd.

items.html: But God prepared a worm when the morning rose the next day, and it smote the gourd that it withered.

blocks.html: But God made a worm that destroyed the gourd.

items.html: And it came to pass, when the sun did arise, that God prepared a vehement east wind; and the sun beat upon the head of Jonah, that he fainted, and wished in himself to die, and said, It is better for me to die than to live.

blocks.html: When the sun rose the next morning, God made an east wind and the sun beat down so hard on Jonah's head, that he fainted, and wished that he was dead.

items.html: And God said to Jonah, Doest thou well to be angry for the gourd? And he said, I do well to be angry, even unto death.

blocks.html:
God said to Jonah,

Do you think it's a good idea to be angry with the gourd? [3]

Jonah said,

Yes, it's a good idea for me to be angry, even to death.

items.html: Then said the LORD, Thou hast had pity on the gourd, for the which thou hast not laboured, neither madest it grow; which came up in a night, and perished in a night:

blocks.html:
Then God said to him,

You had pity on the gourd.

items.html: And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more then sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle?

blocks.html:
Shouldn't I spare Nineveh, where more than 120,000 people live, who don't know their right hand from the left?

And also many cattle.

footnotes.html:
It displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was very angry. (v.1)

Jonah was angry when his preaching converted a city.

God prepared a gourd, and made it to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shadow over his head (v.6)

God prepared a gourd to shade Jonah's head, a worm to destroy the gourd, and then a drying wind and baking sun that made Jonah wish he was dead.

God said to Jonah, Doest thou well to be angry for the gourd? (v.9)

God asks Jonah why he is angry about the gourd. What about the 120,000 people that God planned to kill (along with their animals)? Shouldn't he be angry about that, too?
